comments.text: Astra language ownership planning (2026-08-04; no new product contract): keep the dogfood orchestrator smaller than a framework. Nix owns package composition and wiring; add Rust executable logic only when Nix alone cannot economically express deterministic, typed, checkable Astra-owned behavior. Consume child-repository extension surfaces rather than wrapping them: in particular, Yazi Lua plugins remain owned, versioned, and executed by Yazi, even when Astra selects or pins them. Do not infer an Astra-wide Lua, Python, JavaScript, or Wasm plugin API from a child product. A general extension system remains outside orb-bi4.6. See docs/STACK.md.

title: Choose post-graduation Astra, Venus, and Orbit ownership boundaries
description: After a go decision in orb-bi4.8, choose the sequence and exact scope for expanding the proven one-terminal boundary across the separate Orbit, Venus, and Yazelix Astra repositories. Preserve Orbit as terminal-session authority, Venus as graphical materializer, and Astra as product workspace and orchestration owner. On a no-go decision, close this bead as not applicable.
design:
Three repository boundaries are already chosen for clean ownership, independent histories, forkability, and experimentation. Orbit owns generic terminal-session identities and lifetime, PTYs, authoritative libghostty state, bounded terminal history, terminal effects, and the client-neutral protocol. Venus owns native rendering, interaction, accessibility, and ephemeral view state. Astra owns product workspace topology and policy: repositories, agents, services, launch and resume policy, component relationships, secrets, artifacts, machines, and the mapping from product workspaces to Orbit session IDs.

This bead does not preassign windows, tabs, splits, focus, geometry, or restoration to Orbit. After graduation, route each proposed durable datum to the lowest owner with enough context: terminal-session content stays in Orbit, ephemeral presentation stays in Venus, and product workspace relationships stay in Astra. Define explicit versioned links across repositories rather than duplicating state. A new shared repository, monorepo, compatibility layer, or protocol owner requires another user decision; the default is an Orbit-owned first-party protocol surface consumed at exact revisions by Venus.

Decide multiple terminal sessions separately from Astra workspace topology; restart recovery separately from detach and reattach; remote terminal transport separately from web or mobile presentation; and both separately from remote environment or machine orchestration. Snapshot-plus-patch, history, effects, and resources are protocol decisions triggered by measured need, not automatic consequences of graduation. For every proposed expansion, record observed need, owner, smallest contract, cheapest proof, expected LOC and maintenance, and accept, reject, or defer. Do not create implementation beads until the user accepts that expansion. Multiplayer remains excluded.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The orb-bi4.8 graduation decision is recorded first.
2. After a go, every proposed expansion receives an explicit accept, reject, or defer decision and one repository owner.
3. The plan distinguishes Orbit terminal-session identity and state, Venus ephemeral presentation, and Astra product workspace topology and orchestration without duplicate truth.
4. Multiple sessions, workspace topology, durable layout, restart recovery, protocol evolution, remote terminal attachment, web or mobile clients, and remote machine orchestration are decided as separate slices.
5. Each accepted responsibility defines the smallest versioned cross-owner contract, known consumers, exact update order, proof, portability disposition, LOC estimate, and maintenance cost before implementation planning.
6. Orbit remains the only terminal authority; clients materialize structured state and never become raw-byte replicas unless the separate public-libghostty checkpoint gate is satisfied and the user reopens that choice.
7. Separate repositories remain the default for clean histories, forkability, and independent experiments. A monorepo, fifth shared repository, copied schema, compatibility layer, or new protocol owner requires explicit user approval.
8. Yazelix Astra remains separate from Yazelix Nova; no Mars retirement, Nova migration, or compatibility promise is implied.
9. Crate, framework, transport, and distribution choices remain unselected until the owning evidence-backed gate.
10. After a no-go, this bead closes as not applicable without speculative planning or cleanup scope.
notes:
Current long-term ownership correction supersedes older language assigning durable product workspace topology to Orbit. Orbit owns durable terminal-session state; Astra owns product workspace topology and policy; Venus owns native materialization and ephemeral view state. This is a boundary decision, not authorization for post-graduation implementation.

Use references only for the accepted slice. WezTerm can inform revisioned rows and history; Mosh can inform latest-state recovery limits; Foot can inform local client/server launch and failure separation; justerm-core can inform thin-client protocol shape; zmx can inform session detach and reconnect; librio can inform a separately authorized non-Rust FFI. Amp Orbs informs client-independent product work and orchestration but not Orbit terminal internals. Superlogical terminal multiplexer remains a private, publicly described direction rather than implementation evidence. Remote machines, repositories, secrets, services, agents, artifacts, event wakeups, billing, and multiplayer do not move into Orbit or Venus by implication.

User-selected post-graduation roadmap (2026-08-05): durable planning is accepted for P1 Orbit effects/state separation orb-ll1, P1 Orbit history/selection/copy/search orb-j0m, P2 Orbit semantic command regions orb-3gf, P2 Orbit read-only agent observer orb-p92, P3 Orbit rich graphics orb-j2i, P1 Venus hyperlink interaction ven-lq4, P2 Venus structured accessibility ven-q3w, and P2 Astra session workspace astra-db8.9. These Beads are deliberately deferred. This records chosen planning scope and priority only; it does not activate implementation, edit a contract index, select dependencies, bypass the post-graduation gate, or authorize parallel product frontiers. Each outcome retains one owner and must create separate consumer implementation Beads/commits where a cross-repository proof is required.

Canario at Rio commit 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 is comparison-only evidence for this ownership gate. Its spaces, command palette, CWD routing, quick terminal, and on-demand previews inform Astra workspace and Venus interaction policy. Its same-process librio surfaces and restart-plus-text-replay persistence do not move PTY lifetime or history ownership out of Orbit. The compact shape is the default cost comparator: each accepted extra cross-repository contract must buy a user-visible boundary Canario cannot provide.

## Activation boundary

This is a post-graduation ownership and sequencing decision, not an implementation unit. Select the first authorized frontier and keep the others deferred. Do not fully design or implement every future area in this gate; activated epics must first be decomposed into independently provable child Beads.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Contract routing: ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 remain the only accepted initial contracts. After graduation, each user-approved expansion must first receive a permanent new ORB-C* ID or an explicit approved change to an existing contract before an implementation bead is created. Deferred or speculative multiple-session, topology, restart, remote, web, or mobile scope receives no ID.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Post-graduation language and extension planning (2026-08-04; no implementation authorization): use a Rust center with languages only at natural platform boundaries. A future web Venus should first compare a TypeScript browser shell around the canonical Rust frame decoder compiled to WebAssembly; browser APIs, transport, accessibility, and PWA lifecycle belong to TypeScript, while terminal/frame semantics remain Rust. Do not assume the whole renderer must compile to Wasm. A future Apple-native shell may compare Swift/SwiftUI only after measured lifecycle, input, menu, or accessibility needs justify it around a narrow Rust boundary. Keep web presentation, remote attachment, mobile presentation, and remote workspace orchestration as separate user decisions.

Treat browser Wasm and plugin Wasm as independent decisions. Do not plan a general plugin framework until at least two independently useful, user-approved extension cases reveal a repeated stable capability boundary. For trusted integrations, first compare a versioned out-of-process stdin/stdout request/response contract with no framework. If sandboxing, distribution, or multiple implementation languages justify an embedded runtime, specify host capabilities and lifecycle in WIT first; then run the owning repository's Crate gate across direct Wasmtime, Extism, another credible host, and no embedded runtime. Deny filesystem, network, PTY, process, secrets, clipboard, and persistence capabilities by default.

Orbit does not host arbitrary plugins in its authoritative owner loop. Astra may later own orchestration/actions/workspace-metadata capabilities without absorbing child behavior. Venus may later own commands, status items, sidebars, inspectors, or panels through host-rendered declarative data and events, not raw GPU/window/terminal authority. MCP may later expose actions to agents or tools but is not the product plugin ABI. Each expansion still requires explicit user acceptance, contract routing, compatibility order, and implementation beads under this bead's existing gate. See docs/STACK.md and docs/REFERENCES.md.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Published naming correction (2026-08-05): use Superlogical terminal multiplexer, the descriptor used by Superlogical and Mitchell Hashimoto for the company's first product. The former Logimux token survives only in an append-only historical comment and must not be used in current documentation, issue fields, or future planning.

title: Decide whether Venus and Orbit earn Astra graduation
description: Make the explicit go or no-go decision after the core Orbit contract, minimum Venus client, hardening, and fresh Yazelix Astra dogfood are complete. This decision evaluates the narrow greenfield pair before any optional post-graduation ownership expansion.
design:
Compare the Venus and Orbit path with the current Mars and Zellij path and with continuing Mars Next. Include the closest demonstrated alternatives in the evidence: zmx for a conventional-terminal persistent-session runtime, justerm-core for a structured presentation protocol, and Rio-vt only if a replacement terminal engine was actually investigated. Ratatui, Qwertty, and librio are component references rather than competing architectures. Evaluate correctness, user-visible coherence, presentation fidelity beyond plain text, project-owned LOC, dependency and upgrade burden, measured performance, and Zellij workflows intentionally absent from the narrow experiment. Judge whether the proven boundary can grow into the accepted host-owned durable-workspace target demonstrated by the Superlogical terminal multiplexer, with native materialization by reconnecting clients, without pretending that remote access, multiple sessions, layouts, web, or mobile were implemented. A go accepts Venus and Orbit as the architectural foundation for Yazelix Astra and unblocks orb-bi4.7; it does not authorize modifying or replacing Yazelix Nova, removing Mars or Zellij, expanding the initial scope, further repository restructuring, or promoting channels. The Orbit and Venus repository boundary is already authorized at orb-bi4.3. Venus is a permanent distinct product name rather than a placeholder that inherits the Mars brand. A no-go records what evidence or code should be retained or deleted. Create follow-up implementation or cleanup beads only after the user chooses them.

Canario at Rio commit 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 is the closest demonstrated compact native-workspace counterexample: one SwiftUI/AppKit application owns workspace policy and same-process librio terminal surfaces. Graduation must compare the three-repository and process/protocol boundary against that simpler shape, not only against traditional multiplexers.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Summarize presentation attachment and lifecycle evidence, known limitations, actual Rust LOC, dependency footprint, maintenance risks, dogfood results, measured performance observations, lost Zellij functionality, all remaining P0 or P1 risks, and the relevant reference versions or commits studied across prior beads.
2. State whether Venus and Orbit are materially simpler and more coherent as the Yazelix Astra foundation than building Astra on the current Mars and Zellij chain, Mars Next, or the closest applicable reference architecture. Nova remains a comparison, not the graduation target.
3. State whether the structured presentation boundary preserves rich terminal capabilities or has become an unacceptable text-grid ceiling, and whether it credibly supports the later host-owned workspace target.
4. Obtain and record an explicit user go or no-go decision.
5. On go, unblock the post-graduation Astra sequencing decisions in orb-bi4.7 without changing Yazelix Nova.
6. On no-go, record the retain or delete choice and close orb-bi4.7 as not applicable.
7. Create no promotion, retirement, cleanup, UI-expansion, remote-access, workspace-expansion, or alternative-engine bead without the corresponding user choice.
8. Preserve Venus as distinct from Mars during coexistence and after any eventual Mars retirement unless the user explicitly reopens the naming decision.
9. Graduation audits the immutable proof revision and canonical checks for ORB-C1 through ORB-C7, every accepted Protocol exception, the governance-check result, and every direct or architecture-shaping crate decision and its recorded alternatives.
10. Graduation confirms the Linux-specific runtime surface remains isolated, records every macOS blocker and estimated removal cost, and verifies that Orbit, Venus, and Astra changelogs describe all accepted user- and consumer-visible changes without candidate or internal noise.
notes:
Graduation compares evidence, not feature counts. zmx validates the narrow session-persistence thesis but is not a native Venus architecture. justerm-core is the selected structured-presentation reference, while rio-vt is relevant only as a replacement engine if that choice was explicitly reopened. Ratatui, Qwertty, librio, PTY crates, and renderers matter only through measured component cost. Amp Orbs and the Superlogical terminal multiplexer validate the product value of durable host-owned work resumed by transient clients, but neither supplies Orbit's exact terminal-runtime contract: Amp is a managed remote workspace whose terminal currently uses tmux, while the Superlogical terminal multiplexer remains a publicly described direction rather than a published implementation. Do not score the narrow experiment against cloud provisioning, agents, repositories, services, implemented remote access, mobile product surface, workspace layouts, or multiplayer. Do judge whether its boundary can grow toward the accepted target without a text-grid ceiling. Use docs/REFERENCES.md as the index and implementation beads as the source of recorded versions, accepted lessons, and rejected scope.

Canario comparison: accept its shipped workspace evidence for command-driven navigation, CWD filing, quick access, and on-demand previews. Its persistence path starts fresh shells: SessionStore saves plain-text scrollback, and RioEngine injects it into a new display. It therefore proves a lower-piece-count workspace product, not durable process attachment. A go decision must show that actual detach survival, independent failure, replaceable clients, and authoritative structured state earn Orbit's extra boundary cost.

## Activation boundary

This is an evidence-synthesis and user-decision gate, not an implementation unit. It may update accepted planning and graduation documentation after the decision, but it must not repair product code or absorb a failed prerequisite.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Contract routing: graduation requires an explicit audit of ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 in docs/CONTRACTS.md. The decision must distinguish proved, partially proved, and planned contracts; identify any remaining P0 or P1 gap by ID; and must not treat candidate code or dogfood as accepted proof until the owning bead and its gates are accepted.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Prime-beads graduation refinement (2026-08-04): the final go or no-go must evaluate the actual three-repository boundary cost as well as its ownership, history, forkability, and independent-experiment benefits. It must also record whether the accepted Orbit protocol-consumption shape avoids a mirrored Venus schema and whether ORBF v1 measurements justify deferring or activating a later protocol decision. Graduation does not collapse repositories, create a shared protocol repository, or implement patches, history, effects, resources, remote access, or workspace topology without separate user choices.

title: Extract the canonical ORBF v1 codec for Venus
description: Create the smallest Orbit-owned, platform-neutral Rust protocol surface that lets Orbit and Venus consume one canonical ORBF v1 interpretation at exact revisions without changing the accepted wire contract.
design: Add one dependency-free orbit-protocol package inside the Orbit workspace. It owns ORBF v1 version and bounds, canonical frame data, bounded decode and validation, byte encoding, and complete-frame revision reduction. The existing Orbit server consumes the package while libghostty extraction remains in Orbit; Venus later consumes the exact same package from a pinned Orbit Git revision. Preserve ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 behavior and byte compatibility. Do not add a new wire version, public trace format, fourth repository, crates.io publication, renderer, raw PTY path, terminal state, schema generator, or external dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline records current HEAD, policy hash, Bead revision, ORB-C4/ORB-C6/ORB-C7 routing, intended surfaces, dirty paths, and session identity.
2. A pre-code Reference gate inspects the accepted Orbit proof and every required exact-revision source; a package/dependency gate records the user-approved ownership choice before manifest edits.
3. One platform-neutral dependency-free orbit-protocol workspace package owns ORBF v1 constants, bounds, frame representation, bounded decode/validation, encoding, and strict complete-frame revision reduction.
4. Orbit presentation extraction uses that package and emits byte-compatible frames without changing ORB-C4 or ORB-C6 behavior.
5. Decoder checks reject bad magic, unsupported versions, truncation, trailing bytes, invalid tags/flags/dimensions, allocation-hostile lengths, and stale or regressing revisions within explicit bounds.
6. A canonical corpus generated by Orbit round-trips through the package and includes styled Unicode/graphemes, cursor, alternate screen, title, working directory, hyperlinks, and declared unsupported graphics.
7. The package is consumable from the exact Orbit Git revision without compiling Orbit PTY, libc, libghostty, or governance owners.
8. No external crate, generated mirror, adapter, compatibility window, trace format, command, or additional binary is added.
9. Canonical Rust checks and governance pass; owned LOC, package/dependency footprint, byte compatibility, portability disposition, and remaining gaps are recorded.
10. Touched proved contracts remain partial until an accepted proof-bearing commit, then ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 advance to that exact revision; ORB-C7 remains honestly partial unless its full hardening gap is closed.
notes: User approval on 2026-08-04 explicitly selected the Orbit-owned protocol package and a narrowly scoped implementation Bead after ven-upt.1 reported the missing canonical consumer surface. This Bead preserves existing product contracts; it does not activate Venus graphical implementation.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate — 2026-08-04

Contracts and consumer: this slice changes the owner/proof surface of ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 while preserving their accepted ORBF v1 bytes; it enables Venus VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 without changing a Venus contract. The accepted product proof is e4fde443e625180d7332eff4dff366f64bee30a8 and the pre-edit repository revision is 10a24532c00a8ea11f90055f6ce20858146e42d0.

Required before code:
- Orbit itself at accepted proof e4fde443e625180d7332eff4dff366f64bee30a8 and current 10a24532c00a8ea11f90055f6ce20858146e42d0. Inspected the complete manifest and presentation owner, including the live Extractor/Encoder/OutputQueue path and the test-only Decoder/Frame/read_frame/reattach proof. Independently useful fact: ORBF v1 already has one deterministic complete-frame byte layout and bounded producer limits, but the encoder is private and the only decoder is test-only. Consequence: move the format constants, owned frame value types, bounded encode/decode validation, and revision reduction into one package; leave libghostty extraction, PTY/session authority, Unix transport, and output scheduling in the Orbit binary.
- libghostty-vt 0.2.1, crates.io checksum 6219ed1c364b3ef5815fb0fd2acc0662f792adc706dabf59b7ca89280ee6d066, MIT OR Apache-2.0. Inspected its public Terminal/RenderState surfaces and its global/per-row dirty model. Independently useful fact: libghostty remains the single terminal-semantics owner and can supply complete structured state now plus dirty-row evidence later. Consequence: orbit-protocol must contain no libghostty type or dependency; Orbit alone maps libghostty state into protocol-owned values. Dirty/patch semantics are not introduced by this extraction.
- FrankenTUI at 479436597890a14e82676d0067e3917b2a9de8f5 is routed as required by docs/REFERENCES.md for presentation-proof changes. Its LICENSE is a custom “MIT License (with OpenAI/Anthropic Rider)” that expressly withholds analysis/use rights from OpenAI and agents acting for it. It is therefore license-incompatible for this Codex run: no source, dependency, schema, or implementation-derived mechanism will enter Orbit. Inspection stopped as implementation evidence at the incompatibility. The deterministic transition, headless, golden/property, and one-writer requirements already present in Orbit’s own contracts remain requirements and are independently corroborated below.

Comparison only:
- WezTerm at 577474d89ee61aef4a48145cdec82a638d874751, MIT. Inspected codec render-change types, server change calculation, and client render cache. Stable row indices, seqno-based invalidation, viewport-adjacent bonus rows, and separately hydrated image data are useful evidence that future partial frames need explicit baseline/cache semantics. Rejected for ORBF v1: no multiplexer surface, lazy history fetch, client terminal cache, image side channel, or patch format enters this complete-frame extraction.
- justerm at 0e468a7fde4e75d307983258d09dd8dfbe26f81a, MIT OR Apache-2.0. Inspected its frame/wire map, damage ADR, decoder ownership, and FrameSource seam. Independently useful mechanism: bind consumers to a decoded format-owned frame and reuse the canonical decoder across targets instead of maintaining a second schema. Rejected surrounding scope: no justerm schema, terminal engine, span/damage model, web mirror, WASM package, ack protocol, scroll op, overlay model, or renderer code.
- Mosh state synchronization is comparison evidence for latest-revision convergence and obsolete-intermediate-state reduction. It does not authorize remote transport, prediction, acknowledgement flow control, visible-screen replication, or a new state-sync protocol.

Conditional references:
- cargo-fuzz is conditional only if deterministic malformed/truncated/allocation-hostile checks expose a decoder risk that cannot be bounded economically in normal tests.
- RDP frame acknowledgement is conditional only on measured slow-client pressure that requires receiver feedback. Neither condition is present in this slice.

Rejected as unrelated scope: vt100 and termwiz terminal engines, zmx bootstrap/tail attachment, any client-side VT parser, schema generator, generic protocol framework, compatibility adapter, trace format, remote transport, or renderer.

License result: Orbit and libghostty are project/existing dependency evidence; WezTerm is MIT; justerm is MIT OR Apache-2.0; FrankenTUI is incompatible for this run and contributes nothing to the implementation. No source will be copied from any reference.

Ownership and code shape: a platform-neutral, std-only orbit-protocol library owns ORBF v1 constants, bounded owned value types, strict encode/decode, errors, and complete-frame revision validation/reduction. The root yazelix-orbit package remains the only owner of libghostty, PTYs, sockets, connection order, and extraction. Venus will consume this package at one exact accepted Orbit Git revision and will not mirror the wire schema.

First meaningful contract check: decode the accepted rich ORBF v1 corpus, re-encode it byte-for-byte, reject malformed/truncated/trailing/allocation-hostile payloads before unbounded allocation, and reject a stale or duplicate complete-frame revision while accepting a strictly newer revision. Platform classification: neutral.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Crate gate — accepted dependency and package decision — 2026-08-04

Decision already authorized by the user after the protocol-boundary stop: add one internal, dependency-free, platform-neutral orbit-protocol workspace library and make yazelix-orbit depend on it by path. Do not add an external crate, publish target, schema generator, compatibility window, fourth repository, or second decoder. This gate records the comparison behind that accepted choice; it does not expand the approval.

Affected contracts: ORB-C4, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7; Venus will consume the exact accepted Orbit Git revision for VEN-C1 through VEN-C4. Existing product dependencies remain libc 0.2.189 and libghostty-vt 0.2.1 in the root binary only.

Candidate matrix:

1. Selected — internal std-only orbit-protocol package with the existing explicit little-endian ORBF v1 codec.
Fit/ownership: exact fit; one format owner, reusable by Orbit and Venus, no PTY/terminal dependency leakage, no wire revision. Estimated code movement is the existing roughly 60-line encoder plus roughly 100-line test decoder, with owned public values, errors, reducer, and focused tests added in the same package; no duplicated schema. Cost: one direct workspace path edge, zero external direct/transitive/native/build/Nix dependencies, no proc macros, no generated files. API/versioning: private Git-pinned package, publish=false, explicit VERSION=1 and strict errors; Orbit controls upgrades with its proof commit. License/security: project-owned; checked arithmetic and pre-allocation bounds can match the exact hostile-input contract. Platform: std-only byte/value logic is neutral across Linux, macOS, and a future wasm32 consumer. Accessibility/input/browser: no policy or OS API is embedded, so those remain consumer concerns.

2. Root library target with terminal features, no new package.
Fit/ownership: can expose a decoder but couples consumer resolution to the yazelix-orbit package and its libc/libghostty build graph unless terminal dependencies become optional features. That feature split adds manifest states and makes it easier for protocol and terminal ownership to drift within one crate. Project LOC is superficially smaller but consumer/build isolation is worse. Rejected because the acceptance criterion requires a consumer build that cannot compile PTY, libc, libghostty, or governance code.

3. Keep the encoder private and hand Venus a separate decoder.
Fit/ownership: zero dependency cost but creates the forbidden second schema and makes byte drift invisible until cross-repository integration. Rejected by the Orbit/Venus ownership contract.

4. bincode 2.0.1, MIT (the crates.io latest, 3.0.0, is a deliberately nonfunctional compile_error placeholder and is not a credible candidate).
Fit: mature general Rust binary codec, but its derived representation is not accepted ORBF v1; preserving v1 would still need the owned parser/encoder. Default 2.0.1 adds bincode_derive and unty, with proc-macro/build graph; serde is another optional edge. Owned LOC is not removed for the existing format. Pure Rust and broadly portable, but upgrades/configuration become wire decisions. Rejected: dependency cost and format instability for zero contract gain.

5. postcard 1.1.3, MIT OR Apache-2.0.
Fit: compact/no_std serde format, but it changes bytes and needs serde plus cobs and default heapless support; preserving ORBF again leaves a custom adapter. Pure Rust, macOS/wasm credible, no native dependency, but its embedded-oriented framing and serde data model do not prove the terminal-specific bounds or exact accepted revision. Rejected: more transitive and upgrade surface without removing the canonical codec.

6. prost 0.14.4 / Protocol Buffers, Apache-2.0.
Fit: mature schema evolution and multi-language ecosystem, but ORBF v1 is not protobuf. It adds bytes and prost-derive at runtime and normally prost-build plus a .proto/generated source workflow at build time; that increases build, cache, Nix, and upgrade surfaces and creates generated artifacts. Browser interoperability is strong in a different protocol, but no remote or general multi-language protocol is authorized. Rejected: wire change, generator, schema compatibility surface, and materially greater cost.

7. rkyv 0.8.17, MIT.
Fit: high-performance archive/zero-copy model, but archived Rust layout, alignment/pointer-width choices, validation, and its broad dependency set are unnecessary for a small bounded network frame and make cross-target stability a larger concern. Defaults include bytecheck plus derive and supporting crates such as hashbrown, munge, ptr_meta, rancor, and rend. No native build is required, but compile/upgrade/security review cost is highest of the pure-Rust candidates. Rejected: no measured zero-copy pressure, wrong stability shape, changes bytes.

8. capnp 0.27.0 / Cap’n Proto, MIT.
Fit: explicit schema and cross-language evolution, but requires a new wire and generated bindings; normal development adds capnpc/schema compilation and may require the external capnp tool, creating build and Nix/platform cost. It is credible for a future separately approved multi-language/remote protocol, not for exact v1 extraction. Rejected.

9. Separate protocol repository/package publication.
Fit: strongest physical isolation but adds a fourth version/release/coordination surface and conflicts with the accepted exact-Git-revision consumption model. Rejected by the user-approved scope.

Focused proof and disputed claims: cargo info and normalized crates.io manifests were inspected for bincode 2.0.1/3.0.0, postcard 1.1.3, prost 0.14.4, rkyv 0.8.17, and capnp 0.27.0. bincode 3.0.0 contains compile_error!("https://xkcd.com/2347/"). The accepted e4fde443 Orbit source proves the existing format already has a compact encoder and test decoder, so an external serializer removes no required v1 logic.

Consequences of the accepted choice: Cargo.toml adds crates/protocol as a workspace member and orbit-protocol as a root path dependency; crates/protocol/Cargo.toml declares edition 2024 and publish=false with no dependencies. Cargo.lock should only gain the local package edge. docs/CRATES.md will record this durable decision. Root production maps libghostty state into protocol-owned values; the protocol crate never imports libghostty, libc, sockets, renderer APIs, platform APIs, or governance. The first check is an exact accepted rich-frame decode/re-encode plus bounded hostile-input and strict revision tests, followed by cargo tree/metadata evidence that orbit-protocol has no external dependency graph.

title: Provide host-owned history, selection, copy, and search
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved history contract before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 and any accepted effects contract and changes the client-facing boundary with a separate bounded history/action plane.
- Requires a separately owned Venus consumer contract and exact Orbit proof revision. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

Orbit retains authoritative libghostty scrollback, but ORBF v1 transfers only the visible viewport. Venus therefore cannot provide correct native scrolling, selection, copy, or complete retained-history search without inventing a second history owner.

## Evidence

- `src/main.rs:123-130` configures 1,000 authoritative scrollback rows.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:65-70` states that ORBF v1 carries only current visible presentation and excludes scrollback.
- `docs/RATIONALE.md:93-100` assigns bounded history pages and history requests to Orbit.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md:77-94` records WezTerm stable-row/lazy-history mechanisms and Mosh's visible-screen scrollback limitation.
- `tests/formatter_attachment.rs:261-275` demonstrates that formatted reconstruction does not preserve exact scrollback accounting.

## Scope

In scope:
- Bounded host-owned history pages with epoch-scoped stable anchors and explicit eviction/gap behavior.
- Native viewport gestures in Venus with Orbit-authoritative row contents, selection resolution, copy extraction, and complete retained-history search.
- Visible and history selection across wrapping, wide graphemes, resize/reflow, alternate screen, detach, and pruning.
- An Orbit protocol/runtime proof followed by a separately owned Venus interaction proof.

Out of scope:
- Durable transcripts, machine-restart persistence, command recording, regex or indexed search without a separate measured decision, clipboard delivery policy already owned by the effects plane, and client-side reconstruction of unfetched history.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Before code, add the user-approved history contract and classify the wire change and every known consumer.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: exact libghostty-vt history, tracked-grid-reference, selection-gesture, formatting, and semantic-selection source; WezTerm's stable rows/history fetch and client cache at the routed commit; Mosh's scrollback limit; and one native terminal selection/search comparison.
3. First prove whether the published libghostty surface can traverse retained rows and maintain safe anchors through reflow and eviction. Stop rather than introduce a parallel history model if it cannot.
4. Define epoch/anchor/page semantics, newest-first initial paging, byte/row limits, eviction, alternate-screen behavior, and gap recovery.
5. Keep Venus viewport position and gestures ephemeral. Orbit resolves selection and copy against authoritative state and performs any search that promises coverage of all retained history.
6. Start with bounded literal search and explicit normalization/case semantics only if the user-visible contract can be stated cheaply; do not add indexing or regex by default.
7. Land protocol/Orbit proof first, then a separate Venus consumer against that exact commit.

Dependency decision: existing libghostty and standard library are the preferred shape. Regex, search-index, text-normalization, or clipboard crates require a separate Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral history, anchor, query, and action protocol; native clipboard delivery stays outside Orbit.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if exact published libghostty history or selection APIs cannot satisfy stable bounded behavior.
- Stop if resize/reflow makes an anchor ambiguous without a snapshot/epoch discontinuity.
- Stop for user choice on a breaking protocol revision or public trace/transcript surface.
- Stop if search would require a durable index, unbounded scan, or unstated Unicode semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The history contract is approved and indexed before implementation, with exact affected contract and Venus update order.
2. Attachment remains a coherent visible snapshot; history transfers only through bounded explicit requests.
3. Epoch-scoped anchors identify retained rows until eviction or discontinuity, after which the client receives an explicit gap/resync result.
4. History and selection remain correct for wrapping, wide and combining graphemes, resize/reflow, alternate screen, detach/reattach, pruning, and concurrent output.
5. Orbit alone owns row contents, retained-history coverage, selection resolution, copy extraction, and any search claiming complete retained-history coverage. Venus owns only ephemeral viewport and gesture state.
6. Requests, responses, result counts, copied text, queues, and memory are bounded; a slow history consumer cannot block PTY processing.
7. One strong real-terminal contract test plus deterministic protocol checks cover paging, anchors, selection, search, gaps, and pressure.
8. A separate Venus proof consumes the exact Orbit contract and demonstrates native scroll, select, copy, and search without mirrored history.
9. Locked canonical checks pass and closure records compatibility, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, proof revisions, and limitations.
notes:
Priority P1: native history, selection, copy, and search are baseline terminal usability and foundational for semantic command navigation, structured accessibility, and the agent observer.

Blocked by orb-bi4.7. Semantic command regions and the observer should depend on this outcome rather than inventing their own row identities.

Rejected alternatives: stuffing all scrollback into every frame, formatted-ANSI restoration, client-owned history, durable recordings, unbounded replay, or adopting WezTerm's coupled mux implementation.

Planning estimate: effort L; implementation risk HIGH (history anchors, reflow, eviction, and pressure); confidence MED until the exact published libghostty history/reference surface is proved sufficient.

Canario at Rio 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 is comparison-only negative evidence: SessionStore saves plain-text scrollback and RioEngine injects it into a fresh display after restarting the shell. That is useful visual continuity, but it does not preserve live process state, exact styled history, anchors, reflow semantics, or search ownership. The history contract must not relabel text replay as authoritative history or detach persistence.

## Activation boundary

Do not implement this epic directly. If orb-bi4.7 selects this frontier, create independently provable, repository-owned children for: (1) the libghostty API/identity decision and Orbit history-page contract; (2) Orbit bounded paging and stable-anchor implementation; (3) Venus viewport cache and native scrolling; (4) Orbit-owned selection/copy resolution and a separate Venus interaction proof; and (5) Orbit-owned bounded search and a separate Venus results interaction only after baseline history works. Search must not block usable history and copy.

title: Transfer rich terminal graphics through a bounded resource plane
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved graphics-resource contract and explicit ORB-C6 change before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID.
- Preserves ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 and every accepted predecessor contract while extending the cross-repository presentation boundary.
- Requires a separately owned Venus graphics consumer contract and an explicit compatible-or-breaking update order. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

ORBF v1 explicitly advertises Kitty graphics as unsupported even though authoritative libghostty state can contain image resources and placements. Repeating image bytes in complete frames would be wasteful and unsafe; ignoring them leaves a permanent rich-presentation gap for Yazi previews, image tools, and graphical terminal applications.

## Evidence

- `src/presentation.rs:140-146` advertises hyperlink support and Kitty graphics unsupported.
- `crates/protocol/src/lib.rs:130-135` carries the capability bit but no resource or placement representation.
- `tests/formatter_attachment.rs:224-237` proves authoritative Kitty image state is not recoverable through formatter bootstrap.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:27,65-70` records ORB-C6 as proved with graphics explicitly outside version 1.
- `docs/RATIONALE.md:93-100` routes capability-negotiated rich resources independently of frames and effect ordering.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md:77-86` records WezTerm's separate image-cell hydration as relevant protocol evidence.

## Scope

In scope:
- Capability negotiation and a bounded resource/placement plane owned by Orbit.
- Compare epoch-scoped opaque resource IDs with content-addressed resources; select the smaller correct identity and cache contract.
- Strict type, dimension, byte, chunk, count, lifetime, placement, eviction, missing-resource, reconnect, alternate-screen, resize, and pressure semantics.
- Venus GPU upload/cache/placement through a separately owned consumer proof.
- One real Kitty graphics producer such as a Yazi/image preview in dogfood.

Out of scope:
- A general multimedia framework, sixel unless separately chosen, video/animation breadth beyond the first contract, client terminal emulation, image history persistence across Orbit restart, remote CDN/storage, or embedding bytes in every frame.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Before code, approve and index the graphics-resource contract plus the ORB-C6 change; classify the wire revision and every known Venus consumer.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: exact libghostty-vt 0.2.1/current published graphics resource and placement APIs; the Kitty graphics protocol; WezTerm's resource hydration/cache mechanism at the routed commit; and one real producer used by Astra such as Yazi. Reject unrelated terminal/mux architecture.
3. First prove the public libghostty surface exposes enough resource bytes, placement, lifecycle, scrolling, and generation state. Stop before forks or binding extensions.
4. Compare session/epoch-local IDs against cryptographic content IDs. Content hashing must remove enough retransmission/deduplication complexity to justify its dependency and CPU cost.
5. Keep frames small by referring to placements/resources. Define announce/chunk/request/evict/missing/resync semantics and strict quotas before the happy path.
6. Orbit owns resource interpretation and lifetime. Venus owns validated GPU resources and cache eviction but cannot infer missing placements or decode terminal protocol.
7. Land the protocol/Orbit proof first, then a separate Venus GPU proof and real-program dogfood.

Dependency decision: no hashing, image-decoding, compression, chunking, or cache crate is selected. Every direct or architecture-shaping choice requires the Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral resource protocol; GPU formats, upload, and platform limits stay in Venus.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the exact published libghostty API cannot expose the required resource/placement state.
- Stop for user choice before a binding extension, fork, alternative terminal engine, breaking wire revision, or compatibility window.
- Stop if quotas cannot prevent allocation/decompression/resource bombs before work begins.
- Stop if the first useful program requires a broader graphics protocol than the approved Kitty slice.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The graphics-resource contract and ORB-C6 change are approved and indexed before implementation, with exact Venus compatibility/update order.
2. A negotiated client either receives the supported graphics contract or an explicit unsupported capability; presentation never silently drops authoritative placements.
3. Resource identity, announcements, bytes/chunks, placements, scrolling, resize, alternate screen, deletion, eviction, missing resources, reconnect, and resync have deterministic epoch/revision semantics.
4. Resource count, dimensions, encoded/decoded bytes, chunks, outstanding requests, cache memory, and queue pressure are bounded before allocation.
5. Complete frames refer to resources without repeating full payloads, and a slow/missing-resource consumer cannot block PTY processing or corrupt later presentation.
6. Focused tests cover malformed metadata, oversized resources, duplicate IDs/content, chunk gaps, eviction, out-of-order placement/resource arrival, reconnect, alternate screen, resize, and client failure.
7. A separate Venus proof consumes the exact Orbit revision, validates uploads, renders placement geometry, survives GPU/cache eviction, and requests/resyncs missing resources without terminal inference.
8. Real Linux dogfood demonstrates at least one accepted Kitty graphics producer, including scrolling and detach/reattach.
9. Locked canonical checks pass and closure records compatibility, crate decision, resource measurements, portability, LOC, proof revisions, security bounds, and unsupported formats.
notes:
Priority P3: strategically important for avoiding a text-grid ceiling, but materially larger and riskier than hyperlinks, effects, history, semantics, accessibility, workspace composition, and the observer.

Blocked by orb-bi4.7. It is independent of patch optimization and ordered effects; do not couple those planes merely because both change the protocol.

Rejected alternatives: embedding image bytes in each frame, client parsing Kitty escapes, adopting a general image framework before one producer is proved, assuming content hashes are automatically simpler, unbounded resource caching, or claiming formatter/bootstrap restoration.

Planning estimate: effort L; implementation risk HIGH (resource security, cache/lifetime semantics, GPU consumption, and compatibility); confidence MED until the published libghostty graphics surface is proved sufficient.

## Activation boundary

Do not implement this epic directly. If selected after graduation, create children for: (1) a research spike proving the exact published libghostty graphics API is sufficient; (2) the resource identity, wire, quota, eviction, and compatibility decision; (3) Orbit-owned bounded resource transfer; (4) a separate Venus GPU cache and placement consumer; and (5) real-producer dogfood and acceptance. A failed API spike stops before a fork, binding extension, dependency, or alternate terminal engine.

title: Separate coalescible terminal state from ordered effects
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved effects contract before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID.
- Preserves ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C4, ORB-C5, ORB-C6, and ORB-C7 while changing the client-facing ORBS boundary.
- Requires a separately owned Venus consumer contract and exact compatible-or-breaking update order. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

ORBF complete frames are intentionally replaceable latest state. Bells, clipboard writes, notifications, and similar terminal effects are ordered events and cannot inherit frame coalescing without silent loss or duplication. Conversely title, working directory, and latest progress are state and should not become an append-only event log.

## Evidence

- `docs/RATIONALE.md:93-100` records distinct Snapshot, History, Effects, Resources, and Actions planes and assigns ordered effects to Orbit.
- `README.md:187-195` identifies a separate ordered effect stream as the preferred later direction requiring a user-approved decision.
- `src/main.rs:123-133` installs only the authoritative PTY-write callback in the current owner loop.
- `crates/protocol/src/session.rs:131-168` has no bell, clipboard, or notification server message.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:25-28` proves ordered frames and bounded client pressure but not effect delivery.

## Scope

In scope:
- Classify terminal outputs into coalescible state and ordered effects.
- Add bounded effect identity, ordering, delivery, overflow, detach, reattach, and version-mismatch semantics.
- Capture supported libghostty effects without blocking its synchronous callbacks.
- Keep clipboard and native-notification policy in the highest owner with platform/user context; Orbit owns terminal interpretation and bounded transport.
- Coordinate an Orbit protocol/runtime proof followed by a separate Venus consumer proof.

Out of scope:
- Snapshot-plus-patch optimization, full history, graphics resources, remote delivery, durable event logging, notification history, or terminal effects replayed after an unobserved disconnect.

## Implementation Notes

2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. 5. Define event IDs, revision association, acknowledgements only where they serve a contract, and explicit behavior for queue pressure, disconnect, reconnect, and gaps. Never silently coalesce an ordered effect.
6. Land the canonical protocol and Orbit proof first. A separate Venus Bead then consumes the exact proof and owns native delivery and permission UX.

Dependency decision: prefer the existing standard library and libghostty APIs. Any direct crate or feature expansion requires the Crate gate before manifest edits.

Portability disposition: neutral effect values and ordering; clipboard, notification, and desktop delivery remain isolated Venus/platform concerns.

- Stop if a synchronous callback would require blocking on Venus or user input.
- Stop for user choice on any breaking protocol revision or compatibility window.
- Stop if bounded pressure cannot preserve the selected per-kind semantics without explicit failure.

title: Expose a bounded read-only terminal observer for Astra agents
description:
Contract routing:
- Requires a new user-approved observer contract and explicit ORB-C3 change before implementation; this planning Bead reserves no permanent ORB-C* ID. One interactive Venus client remains the limit while separately authorized, non-interactive bounded observers may coexist.
- Consumes the accepted history and semantic-region contracts.
- Requires an Astra-owned authorization/session-selection contract before product exposure. Planning this Bead changes no contract index or runtime behavior.

## Why

Agents currently perceive terminal work only through ordinary shell access, screenshots, or user narration. Orbit already owns the exact live screen, retained history, title, CWD, revision, and future command regions. A narrow observer can expose that context without hijacking the interactive client or turning Venus frames into a durable log.

## Evidence

- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:22-28` makes Orbit the sole terminal owner and limits attachment to one local client.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:65-70` states that presentation is visible-state replication rather than full history or an observer surface.
- `docs/RATIONALE.md:93-100` separates snapshots, history, effects, resources, and actions.
- `docs/REFERENCES.md:284-291` records VS Code Agent Host's client-independent sessions and snapshot/action reconnection as corroboration, not Orbit protocol authority.
- Orbit `orb-bi4.7` assigns agents and authorization policy to Astra while terminal content remains in Orbit.

## Scope

In scope:
- Explicitly authorized, local, read-only bounded queries for current visible text projection, title, CWD, revision, alternate-screen state, last semantic command/output, and bounded history.
- Exact source revision/epoch metadata and explicit lossy labels for text projections.
- Independent observer pressure, denial, cancellation, and lifecycle semantics that cannot disturb the interactive client or PTY.
- Astra-owned session choice and permission policy through a separate consumer contract.

Out of scope:
- Synthetic input, process control, durable transcripts, arbitrary shell execution, remote/MCP exposure, secret-redaction claims, presentation-frame reuse as an event log, multiple interactive clients, or bypassing the one-owner loop.
design:
## Implementation Notes

1. Before code, obtain explicit approval for the observer contract and scoped ORB-C3 change, then identify the Astra authorization contract and exact cross-repository update order.
2. Complete the Execution baseline and Reference gate. Required before code: exact accepted history and semantic-region proofs; VS Code Agent Host; one local agent-terminal observer such as Wave or Open Terminal; FrankenTerm for lifecycle/security boundaries; and the relevant local Unix credential/permission APIs. References are mechanisms/comparisons, never dependencies by implication.
3. Define a distinct observer role and handshake. It must never claim the one interactive attachment, receive semantic input privileges, or access raw PTY bytes.
4. Orbit owns bounded authoritative projection. Return source epoch/revision and label plain text as lossy; expose structured command/history data only from accepted owned contracts.
5. Astra owns user consent, session selection, and which agent identity receives capability. Orbit enforces the issued local capability or another explicitly chosen local authorization mechanism.
6. Bound observers, outstanding queries, rows, bytes, response time, retained storage, and cancellation. Observer backpressure must not affect PTY processing or Venus.
7. Prove denial and revocation before product integration. Add no generic MCP/remote server in this slice.

Dependency decision: prefer the existing local socket/codec and standard library. Authentication, capability, serialization, or async crates require a Crate gate and user approval.

Portability disposition: neutral query/value contract with isolated local transport/credential mechanics.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if authorization has no single owner or cannot be enforced locally.
- Stop if the feature would weaken one-interactive-client semantics, expose raw terminal internals, or create a durable log.
- Stop for user choice before input/control, remote transport, MCP, redaction policy, or a new service process.
- Stop if observer pressure can delay terminal mutation or interactive presentation.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The observer contract and exact ORB-C3 change are approved and indexed before implementation; the Astra policy contract and update order are explicit.
2. One interactive Venus client remains the only input-capable attachment. Observers use a distinct read-only role and cannot send terminal, resize, lifecycle, or process-control actions.
3. Authorized queries return bounded authoritative data with session identity, epoch, revision, projection kind, and lossy labeling where applicable.
4. Current screen, title, CWD, alternate-screen status, last semantic command/output, and bounded history agree with the same Orbit revision and accepted history and semantic-region semantics.
5. Unauthorized, expired, revoked, malformed, oversized, stale, and cancelled queries fail deterministically without revealing terminal content.
6. Observer count, outstanding work, response bytes, history rows, memory, and time are bounded; slow observers cannot disturb PTY processing or Venus.
7. Deterministic checks cover concurrent interactive/observer access, authorization, revocation, revision consistency, disconnect, pressure, child exit, and Orbit shutdown.
8. A separate Astra proof demonstrates explicit user-controlled agent/session authorization against the exact Orbit revision before product acceptance.
9. Locked canonical checks pass and closure records security model, compatibility, dependency footprint, portability, LOC, proofs, and excluded control/remote scope.
notes:
Priority P2: this is a major Astra differentiator, but it deliberately follows the P1 history plane and P2 semantic command regions so it exposes owned context instead of inventing another transcript model.

Blocked by orb-3gf, transitively orb-j0m and orb-bi4.7.

Rejected alternatives: screen capture/OCR as the canonical interface, handing agents Venus frames, an always-on transcript database, unpermissioned local reads, synthetic keystrokes, general remote or MCP exposure, and claiming automatic secret redaction.

Planning estimate: effort L; implementation risk HIGH (authorization, sensitive data, observer pressure, and ORB-C3 change); confidence MED until the history, semantic-region, and Astra policy contracts are proved.

## Activation boundary

Do not implement this epic directly. After its history and semantic prerequisites, create children for: (1) the observer product, security, and Astra authorization decision; (2) the bounded read-only Orbit observer protocol and projection; (3) Astra-owned capability issuance, session choice, revocation, and consumer integration; and (4) adversarial authorization, denial, cancellation, and pressure acceptance. Input, remote transport, MCP, durable transcripts, and redaction remain separate user choices.

title: Prove a macOS-credible platform seam
description: Before the structured-presentation proof, preserve the accepted Linux-first scope while proving that PTY, process, signal, polling, socket-path, permission, and platform-specific EOF behavior do not shape Orbit core ownership or cross-repository contracts. This is a portability-seam audit and the smallest justified isolation work, not a macOS implementation or support promise.
design:
Start from the accepted Linux candidate and preserve ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 behavior. Inventory every OS-dependent operation before choosing code shape: PTY creation and controlling-terminal setup, child process groups and termination, nonblocking reads and final-output EOF semantics, polling, file-descriptor flags, resize ioctls, signals, user identity, runtime directories, Unix-socket permissions, and stale-socket cleanup. Inspect the exact libc Linux and Apple target definitions plus recorded official Darwin or macOS documentation. Keep terminal authority, semantic input, diagnostic or presentation messages, revision semantics, and future durable state outside the platform boundary. Prefer one small concrete platform seam; do not build a generic backend framework or trait hierarchy for a second implementation that does not exist. Do not implement or claim macOS build, runtime, CI, packaging, or support. If isolation requires a new dependency, material ownership change, or surprising LOC increase, pass the Crate gate and stop for user choice before implementation.

If the inventory shows that the current concrete functions already isolate these semantics, an evidence-only closure with no production refactor is preferable to moving code merely to create a platform module.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline and pre-implementation Reference gate route ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 as preserved or hardened; the Bead creates no macOS behavior contract.
2. The audit maps every current Linux-specific PTY, process, signal, poll, file-descriptor, socket-path, permission, and EOF or error assumption to its owner, core leakage risk, and credible Darwin or macOS replacement shape.
3. Terminal authority, semantic input, client messages, presentation framing and revisions, and future durable state contain no Linux-only value or semantic assumption.
4. OS-specific mechanics remain behind one narrow concrete seam with the smallest justified code shape. No generic portability framework, speculative trait hierarchy, second backend, compatibility layer, or unrelated module split is introduced.
5. Existing Linux unit and subprocess contract checks remain green and prove unchanged ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 behavior after any isolation work.
6. The result records an evidence-backed macOS implementation estimate, remaining blockers, and one portability disposition: neutral, isolated platform dependency, or macOS blocker. It does not claim a macOS build or supported platform.
7. Any dependency or feature change passes the Crate gate before manifest edits and updates docs/CRATES.md with Linux and macOS consequences. Using the existing direct libc shape is also recorded explicitly.
8. A material blocker that would shape the core, cross-repository protocol, durable format, ownership model, or require significant LOC stops for explicit user choice.
9. CHANGELOG.md receives no entry for architecture-only isolation. Any unexpectedly changed accepted user- or consumer-visible behavior is recorded under Unreleased with affected contract IDs and proof revision.
10. Closure evidence records exact sources, ownership and code shape, rejected alternatives, checks, owned LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, limitations, and verification commands.
11. If production, test, or manifest changes touch a proved contract owner or implementation surface, closure reruns the indexed canonical checks and advances ORB-C1, ORB-C2, ORB-C3, and ORB-C5 to the exact accepted proof-bearing commit, or downgrades each affected contract with its gap. An inventory-only result explicitly retains the existing proof revision and does not claim that audit consumption refreshed it.
notes: Accepted proof revision 2b1a8e3ba4a256c3bdb1018c6dc48a8b089193e0. One concrete src/platform.rs owner around direct libc 0.2.189 encapsulates PTY creation and normalized I/O closure, controlling-terminal and process-group lifecycle, resize and descriptor flags, raw polling and neutral readiness conversion, signals, socket paths, permissions, stale cleanup, and socket identity. src/main.rs retains terminal authority, semantic input, protocol, and processing order without libc or poll-descriptor concepts. Rejected for this proof: generic traits or backends, a second implementation, portable-pty, nix or rustix replacement, Ghostty application or thread architecture, dependency changes, macOS implementation or CI, and protocol changes. Canonical checks passed on the proof revision: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (13); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Owned Rust is 1,554 lines, +68 from the pre-bead baseline: main 579, platform 336, tests 639. Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are unchanged. A post-candidate pty-process 0.5.3 scratch build passed the same checks and reduced owned Rust by 44 lines while adding pty-process, rustix, and linux-raw-sys to the normal Linux graph; it remains a credible separate user-approved crate decision, not part of this proof. Portability disposition: isolated platform dependency. A future user-authorized macOS slice is estimated at 0.5 to 1 day and must remove the Linux crate cfg, settle Apple libc compile details, and prove Darwin PTY, process, signal, poll, socket, and cleanup behavior. No macOS behavior is claimed.

Canonical verification after the final edit passes: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (13 passed); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Strict Clippy caught an unnecessary explicit closure drop during the pass; it was deleted rather than suppressed and the entire suite was rerun. Candidate owned Rust falls from 1,556 to 1,554 lines (-2): src/main.rs 589->579, src/platform.rs 328->336 because raw poll storage moved fully behind the seam; compared with the 1,486 pre-orb-pmp baseline, net growth is +68. Concepts and one unsafe representation cast are removed; Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, tests, protocol, behavior, and dependency footprint are unchanged. Rejected simplifications after a second audit: exposing WouldBlock/EIO to core or coupling platform code to Terminal/VecDeque would weaken the seam; combining signal setup would again alter child SIGPIPE inheritance; collapsing process-group teardown, identity-safe socket cleanup, parent ownership/mode validation, final PTY drain, or HUP/ERR handling would reduce lifecycle/security guarantees; a sentinel descriptor was not used because the inspected Apple poll.2 did not establish that assumption. Portability disposition remains isolated platform dependency with no macOS claim. No other concrete bug, omission, or high-confidence simplification remained. ORB-C1/C2/C3/C5 remain Partially proved pending user acceptance and an exact proof-bearing commit; orb-pmp remains in progress.
